implementation.return_type_note: NO canonical return type is claimed here, and that is the honest position. The recovered span contains no RET and leaves no value in any return register on either of its two ways out, so the source-side spelling of the RECOVERED PREFIX is void; but the target's exit lies outside the span, so void is a statement about the prefix and not about the function, and it would contradict the record's return sub-record (register ST0, void_possible false). Rather than pick, this sidecar records the disagreement as unresolved and declares no canonical return_type, so the validator's RETURN SEMANTICS arm reports what the machine evidence actually supports rather than agreeing with a spelling this worker chose.
implementation.receiver_model: ECX carries the receiver and the body copies it once, MOV EDI,ECX at 0x01053be7 (8b f9), which is why the record's shape is R-ALIAS. implementation.receiver_identity: UNRESOLVED and not guessed. No class, no vtable identity, no receiver type, no object size, no vtable-pointer offset, no member and no layout is claimed anywhere in this package. implementation.tail_hop: NONE, and none asserted. tail_call is {present false, form null, target null, after_frame_setup false} in the record this package judges against, and this package re-derives that from the instructions rather than trusting the field. There is no RET anywhere in the 288 bytes. There is exactly ONE unconditional direct JMP, at 0x01053c6a (eb 2a), and its target 0x01053c96 is INSIDE the recovered span -- control flow, not a transfer out of the body, which is the case the validator's own intra-procedural-jump rule filters. implementation.exit_evidence_outside_the_span: Recorded because the question cannot be answered from the listing, and labelled as what it is. That is a CONTINUATION of this function, not a callee. It is NOT used as the basis for any claim the reconstruction makes: the return path, the epilogue, the 0x8 callee-side cleanup and the value left in EAX all lie outside the recovered span and none of them is modelled. Ghidra's own recovered body for this function also ends at 0x01053cff (body_span_bytes 288, size_bytes 288), so a fresh collection of the evidence pack yields the same 95 instructions and the same abstention.
implementation.observed_mechanics_summary: Prologue SUB ESP,0x18 plus four one-word pushes leaves ESP at entry_ESP-0x28 wherever nothing is outstanding, and every stack operand in the body is resolved against that. 0x01053be9 CALL 0x00ffbe50 (no push, EAX); 0x01053bee MOV ECX,EAX; 0x01053bf0 CALL 0x00a1ad60 (no push, EAX). 0x01053bf5 loads entry_ESP+0x4 into ESI. 0x01053bf9..0x01053c05 zero twelve bytes through ESI with XORPS XMM0,XMM0 and three MOVSS stores at +0, +4, +8. 0x01053c0a tests the model word for null and 0x01053c0c branches to 0x01053c6c when it is. On the non-null arm: MOV EDX,[EAX+0x34]; ADD EAX,0x34; MOV ECX,EAX; MOV EAX,[EDX+0x2c]; CALL EAX -- a computed call whose self is model+0x34 -- then three MOVSS loads out of its result stored at ESP+0x10, ESP+0x14, ESP+0x18. CALL 0x00b3d350; TEST EAX,EAX; JZ 0x01053c96; LEA ECX,[ESP+0x10]; PUSH ECX; LEA EDX,[ESP+0x20]; PUSH EDX; CALL 0x00b3d350 (a SECOND time, with arguments); MOV ECX,EAX; CALL 0x00b815a0; then three four-byte stores out of that result into ESI at +0, +4, +8; JMP 0x01053c96. On the null arm: CALL 0x00b3d350; TEST EAX,EAX; JZ 0x01053c96; LEA ECX,[ESP+0x1c]; PUSH ECX; CALL 0x00b3d350 (again); MOV ECX,EAX; CALL 0x00b81720; three four-byte stores into ESI; fall through to the join. At the join, MOV EBP,[ESP+0x30] loads entry_ESP+0x8, XOR EBX,EBX clears the counter and LEA ESP,[ESP] is a four-byte no-op. The loop reads [EDI] then [EAX+0x24], pushes 0x1, ESI and EBP, puts the receiver in ECX, increments EBX and calls the computed word; TEST AL,AL and JNZ 0x01053cf3 end it. Otherwise two FLD/FSTP pairs write 200.0f (from 0x01477fbc) and 50.0f (from 0x013f1cac) to two stack words the span never reads again, LEA EAX,[ESP+0x24] computes an address, two words are pushed and 0x00b3d350 then 0x00b81780 are called, three four-byte stores copy the result into ESI, and CMP EBX,0x3e8 with JL 0x01053ca0 loops. The last two instructions of the span are CMP EBX,0x3e8, JLE 0x01053d3b and then XOR EBX,EBX, LEA ECX,[ECX].
implementation.float_constants: 0x01477fbc holds 00 00 48 43 (200.0f) and 0x013f1cac holds 00 00 48 42 (50.0f), both read back with GhidraMCP /read_memory and both carried in the header as kFarStackFloat and kNearStackFloat; the model test re-encodes them and compares against the image's own words rather than against themselves. Each FLD is consumed by the FSTP that follows it (d9 5c 24 04 and d9 1c 24), so the x87 stack top is EMPTY at every point the recovered span can end -- which matters, because the record's return sub-record names ST0 at APPROXIMATION confidence on the stated basis 'an x87 or SSE instruction appears in the body' (inference RT1), a basis the byte transcript does not support inside this span. Reported as an unresolved question, not resolved here.
implementation.dispatch_model: Two computed transfers, both modelled as computed transfers. 0x01053c19 CALL EAX, with ECX = model+0x34 and no stack words, its result read as three four-byte singles. 0x01053cac CALL EDX, with ECX = the receiver and three stack words (0x1, the out-parameter, entry_ESP+0x8), its result tested in AL. The machine dispatch record counts indirect_calls 2 and vtable_shaped_loads 0, while the 95-instruction listing shows ONE indirect transfer site (CALL EAX); the model test checks both byte forms (ff d0 and ff d2) and the disagreement is reported as a finding rather than reconciled.
implementation.call_sequence_counts: Ten direct CALL sites over six distinct targets: 0x00ffbe50 once, 0x00a1ad60 once, 0x00b3d350 five times (0x01053c3b, 0x01053c4e, 0x01053c6c, 0x01053c7a, 0x01053cce), 0x00b815a0 once, 0x00b81720 once, 0x00b81780 once. The model test re-derives every one of the ten targets from the transcript's own rel32 bytes with its own arithmetic and compares them with literals written in that file.
implementation.callee_cleanup_undetermined: The record's cleanup is UNKNOWN with side null, so which side of each call restores ESP is not established, and this package does not pick. It matters at exactly one place: LEA EAX,[ESP+0x24] at 0x01053cbf resolves to entry_ESP-0x18 (the first word of the local triple) if the computed call at 0x01053cac pops its three words itself, and to entry_ESP-0x24 if it does not. The model passes a scratch buffer there and asserts nothing about that address's identity, and the header records both readings. The other two LEA sites are determinate: LEA EDX,[ESP+0x20] at 0x01053c49 with one word pushed, and LEA ECX,[ESP+0x1c] at 0x01053c75 with nothing outstanding, both give entry_ESP-0x0c, a word below the frame that the span never writes. LEA ECX,[ESP+0x10] at 0x01053c44 gives entry_ESP-0x18 with nothing outstanding and IS determinate, so the model passes the local triple there and the test checks its contents.
implementation.frame_model: The model is written as ordinary C++ and does not reproduce the machine's per-iteration ESP arithmetic, because that arithmetic depends on the undetermined cleanup above. What it does reproduce, instruction for instruction, is the control flow, the twelve-byte write pattern through the caller's word, the call sequence with its argument shapes, the loop bound and the two computed transfers.

implementation.no_bare_assembly: There is no naked-assembly probe in this package, so nothing writes ESI, EDI, EBX or EBP and no callee-saved-register claim is asserted through one. semantic_findings: The recovered span is a PREFIX of a longer function, and everything that would make its ABI decidable lies past it: no terminal return, an out-of-listing conditional exit at 0x01053d3b, and a fall-through at 0x01053d00. That is why the record abstains three times over and why this package declares no convention.

The span writes a twelve-byte single-precision triple through the word at entry_ESP+0x4, zeroing it first and then overwriting it from one of three sources. The zeroing is unconditional; which source wins depends on the model word, on the manager query, and on the loop.

0x00b3d350 is called FIVE times over two arms and a loop, and in both arms the GATE is on the FIRST call's result while the SECOND call's result is what the following callee receives. A reconstruction that passes the first result on, or that calls the manager once, is refuted.
The model-present arm and the model-absent arm are different callees: 0x00b815a0 with two stack words on one, 0x00b81720 with one on the other. Conflating them is refuted by B1 and B3.

The loop's store happens BEFORE the bound is compared. On the 1000th iteration the result is written and only then is EBX compared with 0x3e8, so the caller's word holds the loop's value even on the iteration that ends the loop. B5 pins this.
The loop is bounded by CMP EBX,0x3e8 twice with the INC ahead of the call, so the probe runs at most 1000 times and 0x00b81780 at most 1000 times. B4 and B5 pin both counts from both sides.

The two FLD constants are written to the stack and never read again inside the span. The address the body goes on to pass is a different word. A reconstruction that routes 200.0f or 50.0f into any callee is refuted by the listing.

The x87 stack is balanced: each FLD is consumed by the FSTP three or six instructions later, so the x87 stack top is empty at every point the span can end. That is a byte-level disagreement with the record's ST0 return claim and is reported, not resolved.

The receiver is loaded at displacement zero and nowhere else, and the record enumerates exactly that offset. Nothing is written through it. The word at +0x24 of whatever the receiver points at is a computed call target, but no slot boundary, table identity or class is claimed for it or for the +0x2c word the other arm reads.
Both computed transfers are read out of memory and called through a register. No address is named for either, and no address outside the recovered span is claimed as this span's callee.

The span reads the caller's argument area twice -- entry_ESP+0x4 and entry_ESP+0x8 -- while the record's stack-slot derivation enumerates one slot and carries esp_unresolved true. The record also contradicts itself on the first slot, listing obs-0014 as a STACK_SLOT_READ while slots[0].read is false. The listing is followed; the record is reported, not edited.

This address is the fixture 01053be0_second_wrong_tail_target. Its tail-hop record is empty because the listing has no tail hop: no RET, and the one unconditional direct jump lands back inside the span. The pre-existing tail_call.target field is recorded elsewhere in this repository as provably wrong for this address, and none is asserted here.
unresolved_questions: THE EXIT AND THE RETURN. Both ways out of the recovered span leave it (the JLE at 0x01053cf9 to 0x01053d3b, and the fall-through at 0x01053d00) and neither is inside it, so the recovered 288 bytes cannot say what this function returns. Reading past the span shows MOV EAX,ESI ... ADD ESP,0x18; RET 0x8 at 0x01053d3b, which would return the caller's word and pop eight bytes of arguments -- but that is outside the recovered span, is not modelled, and is not claimed. The true return type, its width, and the callee-side cleanup of 0x8 are all unresolved.

THE CONVENTION. conventions.calling_convention is null with four candidates and confidence UNKNOWN, and cleanup is UNKNOWN with side null. __thiscall is the shape the receiver suggests and is NOT asserted; neither is any other candidate. Which side of each of the six direct callees restores ESP is likewise undetermined.

THE RECEIVER'S IDENTITY. No class, no vtable identity, no receiver type, no object size, no vtable-pointer offset, no member and no layout. Seven classifier vtable associations and 24 xrefs, all at 0x0149b..., are a transitive classifier result, not a class identity, and one address named by several tables is also what table merging looks like. This binary carries no MSVC RTTI.

THE ST0 RETURN CLAIM. The record's return sub-record names ST0 at APPROXIMATION confidence on the stated basis that an x87 or SSE instruction appears in the body. The byte transcript shows the x87 stack balanced (each FLD has its FSTP) and every SSE use a MOVSS pair through XMM0, so the basis does not hold inside the recovered span, while void_possible is false. This package reports the disagreement and claims neither reading.

THE UNDETERMINED ADDRESS AT 0x01053cbf. LEA EAX,[ESP+0x24] resolves to entry_ESP-0x18 or entry_ESP-0x24 depending on whether the computed call at 0x01053cac pops its three stack words itself. The model's ESP arithmetic across loop iterations is not reproduced for the same reason, and the two cases' agreement (the manager opens on the first call, the loop's own manager call is never gated) is a property of the listing, not of the ESP.

WHAT THE WORD AT entry_ESP-0x0c IS. Two LEA sites hand its address to 0x00b3d350 and the span never writes it, so its content is whatever the caller left. It is passed on in the model and never read back, which is the machine's behaviour, and no claim is made about what 0x00b3d350 does with it.

WHAT THE SIX CALLEES ARE. The evidence pack carries NO decompilation for this target (categories.decompilation is missing, and the briefing's DECOMPILATION section says so). The names here carry addresses and nothing else. A cached decompilation exists under tools/mcp/cache/decompiled/, but it is not part of the pack, no claim in this package rests on it, and none of its type names are used. 0x00b3d350 additionally carries a Ghidra name from the SDK surface (Simulator::cGameInputManager::Get) that this package does not adopt as a class, a type or a meaning.

WHETHER entry_ESP+0x4 IS A HIDDEN STRUCT-RETURN POINTER OR AN OUT-PARAMETER. The record cannot decide it (ambiguity sret_vs_out_param, present null, candidates [hidden_sret, out_parameter]) and the listing agrees: the word is loaded into a register and then written through as a twelve-byte destination, which both forms compile to. The entry's second parameter is named for the address it resolves to.

WHETHER THE RECORD'S SLOT LIST IS COMPLETE. It enumerates one slot while the listing reads two words of the incoming argument area, and parse.esp_unresolved is true. Whether entry_ESP+0x8 is a parameter, a reserved word, or an argument the caller does not use is unresolved; the listing shows only that the body loads it and pushes it.

THE DISPATCH SITE COUNT. The machine dispatch record counts indirect_calls 2; the 95-instruction listing shows one indirect transfer site (CALL EAX). Both computed transfers are present in the bytes (ff d0 and ff d2) and the model test checks both, so the disagreement is most likely the record counting the loop's CALL EDX separately -- but that is an explanation, not a determination, and it is not used to change any claim.

WHY GHIDRA'S RECOVERED BODY ENDS AT 0x01053cff. Ghidra holds the JLE edge at 0x01053cf9 as leaving the body, so the body stops one instruction before the code that follows 0x01053cfd. A fresh collection of the evidence pack therefore yields the same 95 instructions, and the abstention is not a stale-pack artefact.

RUNTIME. No original-process trace exists in this repository, none was attempted, and the runtime axis remains GATED at 0. Every claim here is from the disassembly listing, the machine-derived ABI sub-records, and bytes read back out of the image.

Four of the eight structural checks PASS: CALLS (the xref export and the 95-instruction listing name the same six direct transfer targets, with the one intra-procedural jump filtered), CONSTANTS (the listing is consumed 95 of 95 with 0 unparsed and both source constants appear in it), FIELDS/OFFSETS (the source span declares no field offset and the one receiver displacement the listing shows, 0x0, is the one the record enumerates) and VIRTUAL DISPATCH (both computed transfers are found and characterised by the machine parse). FOUR DO NOT, and none of them is something this source could have reached by being written differently: ABI is WARN because the derived record's verdict is ABI_UNKNOWN -- that arm fires before any source-side convention is read, so no source reaches PASS without a determined convention, and this one is not determined; CONTROL FLOW is WARN because one of the six conditional branch targets, the JLE to 0x01053d3b, lies outside the recovered span, so the listing is a slice; GLOBALS is WARN because the complete listing names two data addresses (0x01477fbc and 0x013f1cac) and the xref export carries no data-reference edge type to corroborate them against; RETURN SEMANTICS is NOT_AVAILABLE because the machine return state is SRET_SUSPECTED -- the envelope records an undecided hidden-struct-return hypothesis -- and the source span declares void. mutation_evidence.note: The three SM mutations are the ones that matter for the byte witness: the executed code AND the constants that describe it are changed together, so a case that only compared constants with each other would be silent. SM1 is the sharpest of them -- the emitted behaviour is bit-for-bit what it was, and only A12, which re-reads the image's own bytes and compares them with literals written in the test file, sees the change. Conversely M12, M21 and M22 change the transcript WITHOUT touching the code and are killed by the byte comparison alone, which is the point of pinning the reconstruction to the image rather than to a second reading of the same instructions. FIVE mutations (M1, M4, M15, M17, M18) die at BUILD time rather than at run time: three of them are caught by the entry's own static_asserts, which is where a source that contradicts its own pinned facts should stop, and M4 stops on -Werror. That is reported as a build-time death, not passed off as a run-time kill. NO MUTATION SURVIVED: 25 planted, 25 died.

This is the first revision of this package. It has never carried a calling convention, because the machine record has never determined one; that is the record's answer and it is reported rather than worked around.

The exit question is answered the only way the evidence allows. The record's tail-hop sub-record is empty and the listing agrees; the one unconditional direct jump lands back inside the recovered span, and the span's two real exits are both outside it. The pre-existing tail_call.target field is recorded elsewhere in this repository as provably wrong for this address, and this package asserts no target in its place.

One thing was found by reading rather than by the tooling and is reported rather than fixed: the record's stack-slot derivation enumerates one slot for a body that reads two words of the incoming argument area, and its own obs-0014 contradicts its slots[0].read flag. The reconstruction follows the listing. The evidence pack was not edited.
